title: House on Haunted Hill

evidence.note: Renewal registration RE0000318809 (filed 1986-01-12) exists at the U.S. Copyright Office for a motion picture titled 'House on a haunted hill. By Allied Artists Pictures Corporation.', renewing original registration LP0000012531 (filed 1958-12-29, notice year 1959). The renewing party is listed as Revival Pictures (PWH). The registration date and notice year match the 1959 William Castle film.
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System

evidence.note: The title in the renewal record, 'House on a haunted hill', differs from the film's release title 'House on Haunted Hill'. No renewal was found under the exact title. Whether RE0000318809 covers the William Castle film or a differently titled work is uncertain. Some web sources assert the film's copyright was never renewed, but they cite no Copyright Office record, so they do not settle the question.

The song 'House on Haunted Hill' (music by Richard Loring, lyrics by Richard Kayne) was registered as an unpublished musical composition (EU0000546955, filed 1958-10-20) and renewed in 1986 (RE0000309723, filed 1986-11-17). This is a renewal of the underlying composition, independent of the film's print copyright. A new recording of the song needs clearance from the rights holders.
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System

evidence.note: No separate registration for the film's background score was located. For a sound film the recorded track normally shares the film's own status, which here is undetermined. The Loring/Kayne composition stays separately protected for new performances either way.
The film is an original screenplay with no known underlying novel or play, so there is no source work with a separate term. Its status follows the film's own copyright, which is undetermined.
USPTO trademark records were not searched. No active mark for the title could be confirmed or excluded.

A faithful restoration of a public-domain film adds no new US copyright: copying or restoring public-domain images without original creative additions is not protected (Bridgeman Art Library v. Corel Corp., S.D.N.Y. 1999, following Feist v. Rural, 1991). Anything a restoration ADDS can be protected: a new score, colorization, newly written or translated titles, and other original additions. Separately, ripping a copy-protected Blu-ray or DVD can break the DMCA's anti-circumvention rule (17 U.S.C. 1201) even when the film itself is public domain.
evidence.source: Bridgeman Art Library v. Corel Corp. (summary)

evidence.note: 17 U.S.C. 1201 - circumvention of copyright protection systems.
Modern HD restorations and colorized versions can carry new protectable elements.

editorial:
William Castle's 1959 film puts Vincent Price in a mansion as a wealthy host who offers five strangers $10,000 each if they survive the night. It is a compact black-and-white horror title with a famous lead and a simple premise, and it circulates widely on the Internet Archive. A creator can find ready-to-use copies there. The copyright was registered as LP0000012531 on December 29, 1958 (notice year 1959).

The print is not settled. A 1986 renewal, RE0000318809, was filed by Revival Pictures for a motion picture titled 'House on a haunted hill' from Allied Artists, and that title does not match the film exactly, so it is unclear whether it covers this film. The clear trap is the theme song. Its composition (music by Richard Loring, lyrics by Richard Kayne) was registered in 1958 and renewed in 1986 as RE0000309723. It is protected whatever the status of the film print.
faq: Can I upload or distribute the 1959 House on Haunted Hill?

Copies are hosted on the Internet Archive under public domain and CC labels. Those labels are the uploaders' claims, not a ruling. A 1986 Copyright Office renewal exists under the slightly different title 'House on a haunted hill', so the print status is undetermined. Use a plain copy of the original film, not a colorized or newly scored edition. Weigh the risk before commercial use.
Is the theme song in the film public domain?

No. The composition 'House on Haunted Hill' (music by Richard Loring, lyrics by Richard Kayne) was registered in 1958 and renewed in 1986 (RE0000309723), so it is still protected. Using the track as it sits in the film depends on the film's own uncertain status. Any new recording of the song needs separate clearance.
